dossier.public_summary: The 14.7-day dip shows odd and even depths different by a factor of 5 and a second dip in orbit, plus a depth that jumps from undetectable to very deep depending on sector. The star's strong 8.5-day spot rotation also varies the signal. Together this matches an eclipsing binary blended with the target, not a transiting planet, though centroid imaging was too noisy to positively identify the background neighbour.
